title: Colchis
capsule: Colchis was an ancient polity on the eastern Black Sea coast, corresponding roughly to western Georgia, known to Greek sources as the destination of the Argonauts and the homeland of Medea and King Aeëtes; internally it was called Egrisi by its Zan-speaking inhabitants, ancestors of the modern Laz and Mingrelians. It reached its apogee as a prosperous polity exporting gold, iron, timber, and honey, with Greek becoming a language of coinage and decrees through extensive commercial contact; Greek colonies such as Phasis (modern Poti) established commercial footholds on its coast. By the late 2nd century BCE Colchis fell under the domination of Mithridates VI of Pontus; Pompey reorganized the region following Mithridates's defeat in 65 BCE, and the territory was absorbed into the Roman provincial system, eventually giving way to the successor kingdom of Lazica.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial boundaries of Colchis as a political entity are imprecisely attested; Greek sources describe its general location but internal administrative extent and precise eastern borders remain unclear from archaeology.
